No files were removed, models edited, implementation tests executed or Delivery approved by this assessment. Exact source recoverability, consumer amendments, retained proof and final review/Verify must be established during delivery.

The prior System acceptance sentence about an unchanged usable ledger is original adoption history, expressly superseded for this exact ledger by the current row, cleanup composition and VAL-SR-23. No current retention or duplicate proof duty is inferred from it.
rationale: The governing decision explicitly removes the frozen ledger, reader, test, main.retirement_ledger.regression, fingerprint, routes and exclusive assertions. It retires the private schema, mandatory inventoried/dual-proof transition and historical inventory as maintained behavior; it prohibits recreating those duties in a replacement ledger or synthetic pass. System explicitly supersedes its prior source-tree retention exception and delegates current retirement policy to Validation.

Inspection confirms retirement_ledger.py is a private JSON/schema/invariant module whose actual executable consumer is test-retirement-ledger.py. The suite reads the August 10 fixture and imposes its fixed check IDs, R26 clause set, dual-proof sequence and admission budget. Token-era IDs in that fixture remain historical meaning, not current catalog identity. Retiring the whole obsolete obligation is more coherent than repeatedly updating the frozen inventory.

Two tests touch current state: current_retirement_catalog_disposition_is_explicit and every_top_level_proof_script_is_inventoried. Their historical membership/inventory oracle is retired, but genuine current discovery/selection/catalog safety remains required by TEST-SR-07–10/12 and VAL-SR-03–05/13. Delivery must preserve actual record_retirement.regression, metadata regression, unknown-vocabulary rejection, and complete current selector/executor checks rather than remove the checks reached alongside the ledger.

Current validation_selection.py routes compact-record, selector-preservation and ledger paths through the ledger check. The Design requires coherent catalog/fingerprint/caller removal and retained deleted-path protection without missing-command dispatch. Existing selector unknown-value tests and current record-retirement/metadata protection provide feasible retained boundaries; their actual allocation belongs to Delivery.

The retained published-skill-first test-spec contains historical ledger command and T1/T10/T13/T14 prescriptions. A concise ledger-only applicability notice linking VAL-SR-23 is a necessary consumer reconciliation, preserving historical IDs/tables and independent non-ledger proof. This does not authorize broader spec retirement, spec-read-log deletion or reinterpretation of past review judgments.

Existing System and Validation graphs and necessary supporting views remain accurate: one obsolete check/fixture edge leaves the current catalog/executor flow, without a new component, format, customer migration or permission. Acceptance requires absent selected files and check, retained nonempty current consumer selection, explicit unknown rejection and preserved record/metadata failures. Git recoverability, uncommitted-byte preservation and coherent source/consumer restoration remain required by current cleanup policy.
summary: The scoped historical retirement-ledger removal is coherent and sufficient for bounded Delivery allocation.
